entries: Courses and preparation｜Objectives and materials｜Set the learning objectives, write the syllabus, handouts and exercises, choose textbooks and laboratory equipment, and state the safety and ethics requirements.

Classroom and laboratory teaching｜Lecturing and organising learning｜Lecture on topics such as crop production, plant genetics and soil chemistry, lead classroom discussion, and supervise laboratory and field learning following the procedures.
Learning assessment｜Setting, marking and feedback｜Set and mark examinations and assignments, assess learning progress, and give improvement feedback with evidence rather than a mark alone.
Student guidance｜Academic and career development｜Hold office hours and guide undergraduate and graduate teaching, internship and research work, advising on course and career choices.

Research and funding｜Research, publication and applications｜Conduct research in a specific field, publish in professional journals, books or electronic media, and write grant applications to obtain external funding.

Academic service｜Committees and collaboration｜Take part in departmental and academic committees, admissions and employment activities, work with colleagues on teaching and research problems, and provide professional advice to government or industry.

The three groups are one record each, with no random allocation, replication or other condition-control material; they can only be described, and cannot prove a treatment effect or be extrapolated to field results.

Fixed 8-point scale, R1—R4 at 2 points each, and 0 points for every sub-item not met: R1 gives 2 points if all three groups write the correct 'germinated count/10', otherwise 0 points; R2 gives 1 point if all three group percentages are correct, and 1 point if C−B is written as 30 percentage points; R3 gives 1 point for stating 'these three groups only' and 1 point for stating 'no random allocation and no replication'; R4 gives 1 point for noting the record ID G01 and 1 point for noting that the data are entirely fictional. There is no total pass mark, and the marks are not treated as real grades.

Complete fictional answer scripts: A: 'A=8/10=80%, B=6/10=60%, C=9/10=90%; C is 30 percentage points above B, so treatment C is necessarily effective and can be generalised to the whole field.' B: 'The data recorded in G01 are entirely fictional: A=8/10=80%, B=6/10=60%, C=9/10=90%, C−B=30 percentage points. These three groups only; with no random allocation and no replication, the effect of treatment C cannot be proven or generalised to the field.' A and B are only labels in the task statement and do not correspond to real students.
